Anika: Quick sync — ran a targeted quantization sweep on helix8b-lite with our GTN summarization slice. Wanted to share numbers + a recommended routing holdback for product.
Ben: Love it — short bullets pls, and the deltas we care about (quality, cost, latency, p95).
Anika: TL;DR: int4 gives ~2.9x token $ savings vs int8 but we observe a measurable drop on multi-paragraph summarization. Details below.
Anika: ```
- baseline (fp16/int8 hybrid): p50 230ms, p95 680ms, cost/token $0.0016
- int8-only (opt): p50 220ms, p95 640ms, cost/token $0.0014
- int4 (q4_0): p50 210ms, p95 610ms, cost/token $0.00055
- int4+prune (aggressive): p50 205ms, p95 700ms, cost/token $0.00045
```
Anika: Quality on our 2k GTN summarization examples (multi-paragraph, user length 800-2k tokens):
- baseline ROUGE-L: 42.3
- int8 ROUGE-L: 41.9 (-0.4)
- int4 ROUGE-L: 39.9 (-2.4)
- int4+prune ROUGE-L: 38.6 (-3.7)
Anika: Human-in-the-loop QA (50 samples) flagged that int4 drops factuality in long-context syntheses (~7/50 major hallucinations vs 2/50 baseline).
Priya: Oof. That magnitude on summarization is non-trivial for GTN product (user-visible). Any signal slices where int4 was OK?
Anika: Yes — short-answer and single-paragraph summaries (<300 tokens) maintain parity: BLEU/ROUGE deltas <0.5 for int4. Also embeddings similarity for rerank tasks unchanged.
Evan: So routing idea: route longform summarization to int8/baseline, route short completions/qa/embeddings to int4. How much traffic split would keep unit econ gains while protecting quality?
Anika: If we route ~35% of tokens (the short helpers + embeddings) to int4 and 65% to int8, blended cost drops ~28% (ballpark) vs all-int8. If we can cache prefixes for longform (KV warmstart) we get extra savings ~6-8%.
Sasha: Any latency/regression risk with hybrid fleet? p95 above looks fine but mixing introduces routing/compatibility ops.
Anika: Implementation notes:
- Mark route by request_type + estimated output_length from prompt (cheap heuristic).
- Add fallback: if int4 output fails sanity checks (safety/factuality quick scorer) then retry on int8 sync with token-level budgeted retry.
- Add canary: 10% traffic (product GTN) for 48h, collect scorecard: ROUGE-L, hallucination-rate, latency p95, cost/unit.
Priya: Proposed scorecard KPIs for canary:
- delta ROUGE-L <= 1.0
- hallucination-rate increase <= 2.0 percentage points
- p95 latency <= baseline p95 + 150ms
- blended cost/unit target >= 20% improvement
Evan: Those look actionable. For GTN, product asks that hallucination delta be <1pp, so we might need stricter checks or reduce int4 share.
Anika: Agreed. Suggest conservative pilot: start 5% -> evaluate 24h, then 20% -> 48h, with automatic rollback if hallucination delta > 1pp or ROUGE-L drop >1.5.
ops-bot: deploy-canary helix8b-lite-int4 routing -> started (canary_id=canary-3845, traffic=5%) :rocket:
Ben: For the report to GTN, can we compute cost-per-1000-sessions and token-cost-per-summary baseline vs hybrid? I can do that if Anika gives per-slice token distribution.
Anika: Attached quick distribution (est):
- 45% tokens = longform summarization
- 30% tokens = short answers + completions
- 25% tokens = embeddings/rerank
Anika: With that split and the earlier costs, blended cost/unit ~ -26% vs baseline. I'll put up a short scorecard doc after 24h canary.
Priya: +1 on phased rollout. Add a mandatory end-to-end GTN regression eval after 48h before any >30% traffic shift.
Sasha: Also recommend we run a small adversarial prompt pass on int4 samples (10% adversarial) before promoting.
Evan: Cool — if ops-bot collects the first 24h metrics, we can meet product Friday. Thanks everyone.
Priya: Thanks Anika. Keep notes in the onboarding doc and tag me for the GTN readout.
ops-bot: canary metrics ingestion scheduled (interval=10m) :white_check_mark:
